content: Cemiplimab may interact with other drugs through an unspecified mechanism. Caution is advised, and therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors should be monitored closely during coadministration. Chloramphenicol can reduce the efficacy of cefdinir due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. Cefdinir and the cholera vaccine should not be coadministered. Systemic antibiotics may act against the vaccine strain, reducing its efficacy. Avoid administering the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. Cefdinir may increase the levels or effects of choline magnesium trisalicylate due to competition for renal tubular clearance. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Cimetidine can decrease the levels or effects of cefdinir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin may reduce the efficacy of cefdinir through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents like clarithromycin can inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents like cefdinir. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may reduce the effects of cosibelimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Demeclocycline can reduce the efficacy of cefdinir due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may decrease the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but an alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may reduce the effects of dostarlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Doxycycline can reduce the efficacy of cefdinir due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may reduce the effects of durvalumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base can reduce the efficacy of cefdinir through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate can all reduce the efficacy of cefdinir through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Famotidine can decrease the levels or effects of cefdinir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may increase the toxicity of furosemide due to pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing the risk of nephrotoxicity. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Cefdinir may increase the toxicity of gentamicin due to nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may increase the levels or effects of ibuprofen due to competition for renal tubular clearance. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Ibuprofen/famotidine can decrease the levels or effects of cefdinir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may increase the toxicity of kanamycin due to nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may decrease the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but antibiotics may reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may reduce the effects of microbiota oral supplements due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibacterial agents may decrease the efficacy of bacterial spores in microbiota supplements. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Minocycline can reduce the efficacy of cefdinir due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may increase the toxicity of neomycin due to nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may reduce the effects of nivolumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Nizatidine can decrease the levels or effects of cefdinir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may reduce the effects of pembrolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may reduce the effects of penpulimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may increase the toxicity of plazomicin due to nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. Probenecid can increase the levels or effects of cefdinir due to competition for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may reduce the effects of retifanlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Rose hips may increase the levels or effects of cefdinir due to competition for renal tubular clearance. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Cefdinir may reduce the effects of sintilimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Sodium bicarbonate can decrease the levels or effects of cefdinir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may decrease the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may increase the toxicity of streptomycin due to nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. Tetracycline can reduce the efficacy of cefdinir due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may reduce the effects of tislelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may increase the toxicity of tobramycin due to nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may reduce the effects of toripalimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir and voclosporin may increase each other’s toxicity due to nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Coadministration with drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may increase the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Cefdinir may increase the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefdinir may increase the levels or effects of willow bark due to competition for renal tubular clearance. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Common side effects of cefdinir include diarrhea (8–15%), vaginal moniliasis (<4%), nausea (3%), rash (3%), headache (2%), increased urine leukocytes (2%), increased urine protein (1–2%), decreased lymphocytes (1%), glycosuria (1%), increased alkaline phosphatase (1%), increased eosinophils (1%), and increased platelets (1%). Hypersensitivity reactions have been documented.
